title: Weightwise PD de Rham comparison
as_he_states: Construct the displayed weight-n comparison, with its terminal map an isomorphism onto the kernel; later obtain the evaluated complex through degree n. CL-SA09-137-004; SA09-27/28/29.
plausible_today: For a specified exact category of finite models and an admissible left-exact F, prove a natural homotopy equivalence with good τ≤nF(C•), then separately test products and PD structure. Do not assert unbounded integral reconstruction.
state_of_art: Dold–Puppe1961 §§2-4 and SGA4 XVII5.5 give the homotopical tools; Sullivan1977 Theorem10.1 is rational. No opened source gives the exact full structured comparison.
why_open: The local theorem gives no complete comparison construction; the later paragraph retracts the untruncated wording. The source does not explain a historical abandonment.
worth: High value: an explicit low-weight comparison can determine whether the source’s exact kernel and truncation conventions support the proposed construction.

title: Nonlinear preservation of special complexes
as_he_states: The tensor-closure proposition is extended tentatively to Λ,Γ,Sym and marked false. CL-SA09-137-008.
plausible_today: Retain reduced nonlinear operations on contractible simplicial projective generators; do not expect projective homology after powers of arbitrary sphere objects.
state_of_art: Dold–Puppe1961 develops non-additive derived functors; our exact Γ²K(Z,1) computation gives H₁=Z/2. The problem is resolved negatively for the broad closure claim.
why_open: The manuscript supplies its own false marks; no further historical reason is needed.
worth: Low value as a new theorem: preserve the counterexample and use it to choose the correct domain for later operations.

title: Which Hilbert polynomials are realizable?
as_he_states: For prescribed homology ranks ν_j, at what conditions does a strictly special object with rank polynomial f exist? CL-SA09-137-010.
plausible_today: For finite-support ν_j, the shifted Newton expansion of f−Σν_jbinom(t,j) must have μ₀=0 and all μ_i≥0; construct the finite direct sum of disks and spheres.
state_of_art: The source answers this question; proof_audit.md §1 and outputs/recompute.json check the formula and Euler value. Dold–Puppe §3 gives the rank conversion.
why_open: It did not stay open on the page; the displayed answer needs finite support and the integer-valued polynomial convention.
worth: Low research priority: useful as a normalization test for the companion edition.

title: Extend PID dévissage to Dedekind or general bases
as_he_states: Dedekind à la rigueur; later consider more general coefficient rings. CL-SA09-137-015/019/023.
plausible_today: For a Dedekind domain, replace free coefficients by finite projectives and retain ideal-class and torsion-module data; specify commutativity for symmetric tensor and divided powers. General rings require an exact/projective-complex formulation rather than elementary scalar disks.
state_of_art: The opened PID theorem is Rasmussen–Marchand2019 §3.3; SGA6 I4.8 gives finite-projective complexes over general rings. The invertible ideal counterexample in proof_audit.md §1 proves rank alone cannot be the extension.
why_open: No complete general-base classification is supplied; the source only suggests it. No biographical reason for dropping it was found.
worth: Moderate value: one run can formulate the Dedekind replacement precisely and identify which later universal constructions survive.

title: Complete the intrinsic additive brick category
as_he_states: Axiomatize spheres, disks, extension classes and finite sums; composition is omitted as evident. CL-SA09-137-018/019.
plausible_today: Specify a preadditive category including scalar composition tables, boundary S₀, nonzerodivisor assumptions and an explicit ambient exact structure for Ext¹. Compare its finite additive envelope with bounded PID complexes.

worth: Moderate value: a finite presentation with boundary cases is a tractable editorial and verification task, not a broad new classification.

title: Recover tensor and Γ operations on coefficient functors
as_he_states: La chose restante à faire and Notre propos principal ask to express F(M)⊗F(N)→F(M⊗N) and Γ^iF(M)→F(Γ^iM) as extra cochain structure. CL-SA09-137-023/039/040.
plausible_today: Define the strict operations and all units, substitutions and naturality maps on a precise admissible functor category; prove extension from generators before comparing to an operadic model.

worth: Very high value: resolving the local extension and coherence data is the necessary first step toward every reconstruction comparison.

title: Density, dual density and restriction of functors
as_he_states: The canonical presentation and restricted nerve are identified with generation by colimits; restriction of colimit-preserving functors is marked à vérifier, with an equivalence clause deleted. CL-SA09-137-020/021/022.
plausible_today: Use canonical density and codensity, or the finite additive-enriched envelope. Restriction is fully faithful when the indicated canonical presentations are preserved, and the finite additive case is a matrix equivalence.
state_of_art: Isbell1960 introduction and §1.3-1.5 supply the adequate-subcategory and conjugacy framework. Our scalar-homogeneous nonadditive map disproves the weaker Set-valued finite-sum shortcut.
why_open: The handwritten verification is omitted and one overstrong claim is false; the standard correction was already available.
worth: Moderate editorial value: identify the intended enriched statement and limits, but do not market it as a new higher-density theorem.

title: Compare structured cochains with de Rham data in both directions
as_he_states: Il faudrait examiner whether de Rham–Sullivan or PD de Rham determines the supplementary structure; the reverse direction is called clear. CL-SA09-137-024/042.
plausible_today: Over Q-algebras, compare fully specified structured cochains with an appropriate rational CDGA model; integrally specify a PD/enriched category and weak equivalences, and prove separate functors and inverse comparisons.
state_of_art: Sullivan1977 Theorem10.1 supplies the rational homotopy benchmark. Horel Theorem5.4, Mandell MainTheorem and Toën Theorem0.1 use distinct integral enhancements and do not identify this precise datum.
why_open: Neither direction is constructed on the leaf; characteristic0 is too short a hypothesis for factorial arguments. No source explains why the author stopped here.
worth: Very high interest but limited one-run reach: begin with one exact functor and low-degree operation compatibility.

title: How much homotopy type do the supplementary operations recover?
as_he_states: Il faut voir dans quelle mesure the structure reconstructs the homotopy type. No connectivity or finiteness class is specified. CL-SA09-137-024.
plausible_today: Distinguish conservativity, recognition of objects, recovery of mapping spaces and inverse realization; test a specified model on connected nilpotent finite-type spaces before widening scope.
state_of_art: Sullivan1977 Theorem10.1 is rational; Mandell2006 is faithful and recognizes integral finite-type nilpotent objects but not full; Horel2024 Theorems5.4/6.1 gives binomial recovery/integral completion; Toën2020 Theorem0.1 is simply connected finite type.
why_open: PursuingStacks§119 reports failure of a particular later divided-power-derived comparison and proposes a binomial alternative; it is not a blanket retraction of this question.
worth: High long-term interest: a few hours can isolate the correct source category and test K(Z,1), K(Z,2) and torsion examples, not prove the whole programme.

title: Freeness versus Karoubi completion
as_he_states: A cancelled Karoubian claim is followed by admitting that every finite-free summand is free; later an idempotent-complete target is required. CL-SA09-137-026/029.

state_of_art: SGA6 I4.8 treats finite projectives; Bühler§6 gives idempotent completion; Dold–Puppe normalization uses split idempotents in additive targets.
why_open: The text itself flags the freeness hypothesis, which fails over product rings.
worth: Low novelty, high editorial priority: resolve the chosen category before any universal theorem is stated.
